02

Service catalogue — one workspace, any operation

You define the workspace. A workspace is the operational domain you choose to run — a city, a plant, a fleet, a programme, a theatre. Name its nouns, point it at the sources you already operate, and the same six services apply.

01 · ConnectOne event contract for every source

HTTP ingest plus browser, React, Node, Python, Java, Go, Swift and Android SDKs. Per-event validation; 1,000 events per request, 1 MB body.

02 · ModelOntology in your own nouns

Define entities, fields and relations for the domain you operate. Populated from event group keys, or marked needs a connector; versioned and audited.

03 · GovernGoverned metrics, one number

Promote an analysis to a named, owned, versioned metric. Dashboards, alerts and answers all resolve through that single definition.

04 · WatchDetectors, cases and alerts

Champion and challenger models judge your entities at cadence and raise cases; threshold alerts are evaluated every minute, with state and history.

05 · AnalyseJourneys, segments and root cause

Funnels, paths, retention, cohorts, segments, acquisition and deep analysis — including readings that are only unusual together.

06 · AskAsk in English, see the query

A question becomes a visible, auditable query over your entities. Only schemas and the question reach the model — never raw events.

03

Fundamental Introduction

From fragmented telemetry to self governed operational decisions

Operations do not lack data. They lack a single, trusted path from a sensor reading to a number a institution will act on.

  • One event contract — every asset, reading, alarm and work order arrives through the same ingest path.
  • One entity model — assets, sites, users and accounts are first-class nouns, versioned and auditable.
  • One governed number — metrics are named, owned and versioned, deterministic so two people asking get the same answer.
  • One AI path — the model sees schemas and questions, NEVER raw operational data.
04

Why now: the industrial data-to-AI gap

The gap is trust and continuity, not connectivity

Fragmented

SCADA (Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition), historians, ERPs(Enterprise resource planning) and spreadsheets each hold a partial truth. Modern Systems struggle with reconciliation.

Disconnected

Bridges buffer readings for hours; a batch flushed late must still land on the right minute.

Ungoverned

Two dashboards, two definitions, two numbers. Decisions stall on whose number is right.

AI-shy

Teams expect insight but will not ship raw operational data to a model vendor.

05

Platform architecture

Ingest → Ontology → Governed metrics → AI insight

1 · Ingest

One HTTP contract for every SDK. Per-event validation, at-least-once delivery, de-duplication on a stable client id.

2 · Ontology

Assets, sites, users and accounts materialised from the event stream, with relations and versioned fields.

3 · Governed metrics

Named, owned, versioned definitions. Dashboards, alerts and AI all read the same number.

4 · AI insight

Questions become AUDITABLE queries. Raw events never leave the workspace.

06

Real-time ingestion and edge reliability

Built for the hard network, not the lab network

  • Per-event validation — one malformed event never loses the other 999; the response names each refusal by index.
  • At-least-once + de-duplication — retrying is always safe when every event carries a stable id.
  • Quarantine, not silence — an event that cannot be stored is held with its state/stage and reason.
  • Bounded queues & backoff — SDKs batch, retry with exponential backoff and jitter, and drop only when the budget is exhausted.
  • Restart survival differs — browser and Swift persist; server SDKs hold queues in memory. Design the bridge accordingly.

Operational limits are explicit: 1,000 events per request, 1 MB body, a per-key ingestion budget.

07

Entity graph and ontology modeling

Your nouns, defined once

Tangent describes your operation in your nouns — "Asset, Site, Account, User, Release, Work order, Actuations, etc." — and every analysis and AI answer is limited to nouns you have configured in your workspace has defined.

  • Entities are populated from events or clearly marked needs a connector.
  • Labels, descriptions and fields are versioned; every save is audited.
  • Your defined Relations turn a flat stream into a graph you can filter and traverse.
  • Assets appear from a single group key on the event — no connector required.
08

Governed metrics and the trust layer

One definition, one owner, one number

  • Promote to metric — an analysis becomes a named, versioned definition.
  • Ownership is mandatory — a metric without an owner cannot be published.
  • Changes are versions — the previous definition is kept and pinned consumers are notified.
  • One path — dashboards, alerts and Ask-in-English all resolve through the governed definition.

09

Domain Example : Mining — heavy equipment, site safety, extraction tracking

Mining

Operational problem

Fleet health and safety depend on readings from remote sites that report intermittently and inconsistently.

Ingestion

One rolled-up sensor_reading per asset per interval; alarms and trips as their own events; a maintenance intervention as a work order.

Entity model

Asset as the group key; site as a property; manufacturer, model and criticality lifted onto the asset profile.

Governed metrics

Alarm rate per asset, vibration excursions, time-to-work-order, quiet-asset count.

AI insight

Unprompted anomaly scan compares today with the asset's own history; work orders assessed at fixed checkpoints.

ROI outcome

Fewer unplanned stops, faster intervention, auditable safety trails.

10

Domain Example : Manufacturing — IIoT streams, defects, cycle time

Manufacturing & assembly line

Operational problem

Line performance is buried across PLCs, historians and quality systems that never share a timeline.

Ingestion

Interval-based readings per station, defect events with reason codes, maintenance as work orders.

Entity model

Line and station as entities; part and batch as properties; operator as user.

Governed metrics

OEE components, defect rate, cycle-time variance, maintenance effectiveness.

AI insight

Ask-in-English over machine and quality schemas; segment scan for what moved a metric.

ROI outcome

Higher OEE, lower scrap, shorter changeover.

Domain Example : Social causes & non-profit impact tracking

Social impact & non-profit

Operational problem

Funders demand proof of outcome, but beneficiary data is sensitive and scattered across programmes.

Ingestion

Programme events, beneficiary identity with consent, resource allocation and outcome attestations.

Entity model

Beneficiary, programme, cohort, funder — with privacy and consent fields first-class.

Governed metrics

Reach, completion, cost-per-outcome, retention of beneficiaries.

AI insight

Only schemas leave the workspace, so sensitive beneficiary data stays put.

ROI outcome

Defensible impact reporting and better resource allocation.

Domain Example : Retail & supply chain

Retail & supply chain

Operational problem

Omnichannel journeys, inventory and fulfilment span systems with no shared customer identity.

Ingestion

Orders, carts, product views; revenue objects; group memberships; device context.

Entity model

Shopper, account, product, order; customer entity resolution across sessions.

Governed metrics

Conversion, basket, repeat purchase, campaign return, inventory turns.

AI insight

Root-cause scan across channel, campaign and product segments.

Domain Example : Oil & Gas — pipeline telemetry, integrity, compliance

Oil & Gas

Operational problem

Upstream and downstream assets report across harsh, low-bandwidth links; integrity and safety evidence must be defensible.

Ingestion

Pressure, temperature, flow and vibration readings; alarms as events; work orders as interventions.

Entity model

Well, pipeline segment, facility and asset as entities; contract as group membership.

Governed metrics

Integrity index, alarm-to-intervention time, throughput, compliance evidence completeness.

AI insight

Change-point and multivariate detection on named features; explanation of what moved.

ROI outcome

Reduced leak risk, faster response, audit-ready compliance.

14

Domain Example : Military & Defense — secure edge, tactical tracking

Military & Defense

Operational problem

Mission data arrives over low-bandwidth, intermittent links from dispersed assets, and must be trustworthy under degraded conditions.

Ingestion

Compact readings and alarms from field bridges; stable ids; chunked batches; backoff on budget.

Entity model

Tactical asset, unit and mission as entities; readiness state as a property.

Governed metrics

Asset readiness, mission tempo, logistics latency, anomaly count.

AI insight

Bring-your-own-endpoint tier keeps everything inside the accredited network.

ROI outcome

Faster decisions in degraded comms; demonstrable data sovereignty.
